```text
1	# PLM to Wrike Sync
2	
3	One-way synchronisation of product data from a PLM source database into Wrike work items.
4	The pipeline runs as three Azure Functions (two core sync functions plus a reconciliation function)
5	decoupled by an Azure Service Bus queue, so each record is processed and retried independently
6	and a single bad record never stops the batch.
7	
8	## What it does
9	
10	- Reads product records that changed since the last run from a PostgreSQL source table.
11	- Selects one canonical record per product family (CORE preferred over CUSTOM).
12	- Creates a Wrike card for a new family, or updates the existing card for a known family via a
13	  1:1 live map (PLM record ↔ Wrike card keyed by id).
14	- On update, writes only the fields that actually changed, merges the PLM-owned description
15	  sections, comments on tracked content changes, and raises a comment-only alert on fields
16	  that must not be auto-overwritten.
17	- Routes unmapped or ambiguous cards to a human-reviewed log table, exported to Excel for
18	  data-quality review.
19	- Records the outcome of every record in a sync-state table and routes repeated failures to
20	  a dead-letter queue.
21	
22	The sync is one directional, from PLM to Wrike. Wrike is never read back as a source of truth
23	beyond confirming the current state of a card before an update.
24	
25	## Architecture
26	
27	```
28	PostgreSQL (source)
29	   -> Producer Function (timer)        reads the change delta, enqueues one message per family
30	   -> Service Bus queue (plm-sync)     decouples and buffers, with a dead-letter queue
31	   -> Consumer Function (queue trigger) transforms and writes to Wrike, records sync state
32	   -> Wrike API                        creates or updates the card
33	   -> PostgreSQL (sync state)          family to card map, watermark, dead-letter, unmapped log
34	   -> Reconciliation Function (HTTP)   on-demand full-folder audit of unmapped cards
35	```
36	
37	| Azure resource | Role |
38	|---|---|
39	| Function App (Python) | Hosts three functions: producer (timer), consumer (queue trigger), reconciliation (HTTP) |
40	| Service Bus namespace and queue | Decoupling, retry, and dead-lettering between producer and consumer |
41	| PostgreSQL | Source records, sync state, live map, folder routing, and unmapped-card log |
42	| Key Vault | Wrike tokens, database connection string, Service Bus connection string |
43	| Application Insights | Execution logs, failures, and queue metrics |
44	
45	## How it works
46	
47	### Producer (timer trigger)
48	
49	Runs on a schedule (`0 0 12,0 * * *`, which is 12:00 and 00:00 UTC, or 05:00 and 17:00
50	Pacific). On each run it:
51	
52	1. Reads the watermark, then selects records where `modified_at` is later than the watermark
53	   and the eligibility flag is set.
54	2. Reduces each family to its canonical record.
55	3. Sends one Service Bus message per family. The message carries identifiers only, not a data
56	   snapshot, so the consumer always acts on the current database state.
57	4. Advances the watermark once the messages are enqueued. Delivery and retry are then owned by
58	   the queue.
59	
60	The producer does not call Wrike.
61	
62	### Consumer (Service Bus queue trigger)
63	
64	Triggers once per message. For each message it:
65	
66	1. Re-reads the canonical family by identifier. If the family is no longer eligible, the
67	   message is acknowledged and skipped.
68	2. Decides create or update using a three-step resolution:
69	   - If the family has a live map row, update that card directly by id (no Wrike search).
70	   - Otherwise, search Wrike by the "PLM - Item #" custom field within the prefix's mapped folder.
71	   - Branch based on the search result: nothing → create; one exact match → update; extras or
72	     non-exact → log to the review table.
73	3. Builds the Wrike payload and writes the card (if the branch is create or update).
74	4. Records the result in the sync-state table and the unmapped-log table (if applicable).
75	
76	An unhandled error abandons the message lock, so Service Bus redelivers it and, after the
77	maximum delivery count, moves it to the dead-letter queue.
78	
79	### Reconciliation (HTTP trigger, on demand)
80	
81	The `plm_wrike_reconcile` function (route `/api/reconcile`, auth level FUNCTION) performs a
82	full-folder audit: it walks every card in each managed folder (including the staging folder)
83	and attempts to match each card to a PLM record by item number + raw customer string. Cards
84	that do not match—including hand-made cards—are logged to the unmapped-log table for the
85	client's data-quality review. The function is read-only against Wrike and run on demand
86	(e.g., after a cold-start or to audit the folder state).
87	
88	## Field mapping and sync rules
89	
90	- Create payload carries the full field set. Update payload carries only update-eligible
91	  custom fields whose incoming value differs from the live card.
92	- Create-only fields (for example brand category, customer, design brief, image link) are set
93	  once at creation and never overwritten on update.
94	- The description is section-merged on update, not replaced. Only the PLM-owned sections are
95	  refreshed.
96	- A change to a tracked content field (material codes, contents) is written and a summary
97	  comment is added to the card.
98	- A change to a protected field (title, brand category) is not written. A comment-only alert
99	  is posted instead.
100	- Every new card is stamped with the Wrike Item Type "Retail Item".
101	- A card with no real change is left untouched.
102	- Customer matching is raw and exact (no normalization)—deliberately surfaces data-quality
103	  issues so they land in the Excel export for client review.
104	
105	The Wrike author of a card is the owner of the API token that created it. Tokens are mapped to
106	product categories in the `category_author_map` table. Cards are placed in the folder identified
107	by the `wrike_folder_map` table (prefix → folder id), and a family with an unmapped prefix is
108	created in the staging folder (a special `'*'` row in `wrike_folder_map`) and the missed prefix
109	is logged.
110	
111	## Data model
112	
113	The schema is defined in `db/schema.sql`.
114	
115	| Table | Purpose |
116	|---|---|
117	| `plm_item` | Source records, one row per PLM variant |
118	| `category_author_map` | Product category to author token mapping |
119	| `sync_watermark` | Incremental cursor and last-run statistics |
120	| `wrike_task_map` | 1:1 live map (PLM record ↔ Wrike card); keys: `plm_internal_id` (PK) ↔ `wrike_task_id` (UNIQUE); columns `item_number`, `family_id`, `customer` for audit/recovery |
121	| `wrike_folder_map` | Item prefix to folder routing table (human-maintained, sole authority); keys: `prefix` (PK), columns `wrike_folder_id`, `full_folder_name`, `space_id`, timestamps |
122	| `wrike_unmapped_log` | Review log for unmapped, ambiguous, or hand-made cards; columns: `item_number`, `customer`, `wrike_task_id`, `prefix`, `reason` (e.g., `no_exact_match`, `multiple_exact_matches`, `non_identical_extra`, `unmapped_prefix`, `no_plm_match`), `details`, `created_at` |
123	| `sync_dlq` | Records that failed after retries |
124	
125	## Configuration
126	
127	All configuration is supplied through Function App application settings. Secrets are stored in
128	Key Vault and referenced from the settings, so no secret value is held in the application
129	configuration itself.
130	
131	| Setting | Purpose | Source |
132	|---|---|---|
133	| `PG_CONN` | PostgreSQL connection string | Key Vault reference |
134	| `ServiceBusConnection` | Queue listener connection (consumer) | Key Vault reference |
135	| `ServiceBusSendConnection` | Queue sender connection (producer) | Key Vault reference |
136	| `ServiceBusQueue` | Queue name, default `plm-sync` | Plain value |
137	| `WRIKE_TOKEN_<NAME>` | Wrike API token per author identity | Key Vault reference |
138	| `WRIKE_HOST` | Wrike API host, default `www.wrike.com` | Plain value |
139	| `WRIKE_RETAIL_ITEM_TYPE_ID` | Custom Item Type id for new cards | Plain value |
140	| `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` | Telemetry | Plain value |
141	
142	The `WRIKE_TOKEN_<NAME>` setting names must match the `token_ref` values in
143	`category_author_map`. Folder routing is read from the `wrike_folder_map` table; the app
144	never searches Wrike for folders by name. A special `'*'` row in `wrike_folder_map` serves as
145	a fallback staging folder for unmapped prefixes. If no `'*'` row is present, items with
146	unmapped prefixes defer (safe degradation).
147	
148	## Deployment using the Azure portal
149	
150	1. Resource group. Create a resource group to hold all resources.
151	
152	2. PostgreSQL. Create an Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. Apply `db/schema.sql`
153	   to create the tables. Load the source records into `plm_item`.
154	
155	3. Service Bus. Create a Service Bus namespace on the Standard tier. Add a queue named
156	   `plm-sync` and set maximum delivery count to 10, enable dead-lettering on message
157	   expiration, and enable duplicate detection. The dead-letter queue is created automatically.
158	
159	4. Key Vault. Create a Key Vault. Add the Wrike tokens, the PostgreSQL connection string, and
160	   the Service Bus connection string as secrets.
161	
162	5. Function App. Create a Function App with the Python runtime. Open Identity and enable the
163	   system-assigned managed identity. In the Key Vault access policies, grant that identity Get
164	   and List on secrets.
165	
166	6. Application settings. Open Configuration on the Function App and add the settings in the
167	   table above. For each secret, use a Key Vault reference of the form
168	   `@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/secrets/<name>/)`.
169	
170	7. Networking, if the database is private. Add VNet integration on the Function App and place
171	   the database behind a network rule that allows access from the function subnet only.
172	
173	8. Deploy the code. Publish this project to the Function App using the Azure Functions
174	   extension for Visual Studio Code, the Azure Functions Core Tools, or the portal Deployment
175	   Center. After deployment, three functions appear under Functions: `plm_wrike_producer`
176	   (timer), `plm_wrike_consumer` (queue trigger), and `plm_wrike_reconcile` (HTTP).
177	
178	9. Folder mapping. Populate the `wrike_folder_map` table with the item prefixes and their
179	   target folder ids (e.g., WP → 4459532498, LT → 4469574468). New prefixes are added by
180	   humans after client/business approval, not by the app.
181	
182	10. Verify. On the Function App, confirm the host is running and all three functions are listed.
183	    On Configuration, confirm every Key Vault reference shows a resolved status. Test the
184	    producer and consumer by running the producer manually (via Code and Test or admin endpoint)
185	    and checking the queue depth and logs.
186	
187	## Operations
188	
189	- Run on demand. The producer runs automatically on its schedule. To run it immediately,
190	  open the `plm_wrike_producer` function in the portal and use Code and Test, then Run, or
191	  call the function admin endpoint with the host key. `scripts/trigger_azure.sh` wraps the
192	  command-line equivalents for triggering, checking queue depth, and tailing logs.
193	
194	- Reconciliation audit. To audit the managed folders for unmapped or hand-made cards,
195	  call the `plm_wrike_reconcile` HTTP function (route `/api/reconcile`). The function is
196	  read-only and logs every unmapped card to the review table for export.
197	
198	- Monitor. Use Application Insights for execution logs and failures. Use the Service Bus
199	  metrics for active and dead-lettered message counts.
200	
201	- Failures. A record that fails all retries lands in the queue dead-letter sub-queue and is
202	  recorded in `sync_dlq`. Configure an alert on a dead-letter count greater than zero so a
203	  record that never reached Wrike is noticed.
204	
205	- Data-quality review. Export the `wrike_unmapped_log` table to Excel to review unmapped,
206	  ambiguous, and hand-made cards. The table includes the item number, customer, Wrike task id,
207	  prefix, reason code, and details for each unmapped card.
208	
209	## Local development
210	
211	A local environment is provided for running the test suite. It is not required for the Azure
212	deployment.
213	
214	1. Set up a local PostgreSQL instance with a `plm` database and `plm` role. The defaults
215	   are `localhost:5432`, `db plm`, `user plm`, `password plm_local_pw`. To override, set
216	   any of `PG_HOST`, `PG_PORT`, `PG_DB`, `PG_USER`, `PG_PASSWORD`, or use a single `PG_CONN`
217	   connection string.
218	
219	2. Apply the schema (idempotent, includes guarded migrations):
220	
221	```
222	psql -h localhost -U plm -d plm -f db/schema.sql
223	```
224	
225	3. Optionally load the sample data:
226	
227	```
228	psql -h localhost -U plm -d plm -f seed_plm_item.sql
229	```
230	
231	4. Run the test suite:
232	
233	```
234	python -m pytest
235	```
236	
237	Tests automatically skip database-backed cases if PostgreSQL is unreachable. Note that tests
238	truncate the state tables during execution. Before running a live sync batch after tests,
239	reload the seed data to reset the sync state.
240	
241	The application reads settings locally from `local.settings.json`, which is excluded from
242	version control. Use `local.settings.json.example` as a template.
243
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# 002 Centric 8 API as the PLM Source
2	
3	**Status:** approved
4	**Created:** 2026-06-11
5	**Last updated:** 2026-06-11
6	
7	> Builds on **001** (the as-built PLM → Wrike sync). 001 is unchanged by this spec
8	> except for *where `plm_item` rows come from*. Read 001 first for the engine this
9	> feeds.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. Overview
14	
15	Today `plm_item` (the sync source) is loaded from an Excel `Wrike` sheet / synthetic
16	CSV by `loader.py`. This spec replaces that source with the **live Centric 8 PLM REST
17	API**: a new Centric client fetches product *styles* and a refresh step maps each into
18	a `plm_item` row and upserts it into Postgres. Postgres stays as both the **state**
19	store (watermark, task map, folder/author maps, dead-letter, review log — all 001) and
20	a **mirror** of the Centric source. The producer/Service Bus/consumer/reconcile engine
21	from 001 reads that mirror exactly as before — none of it changes.
22	
23	## 2. Requirements
24	
25	**Centric client (`centric_client.py`)**
26	- WHEN the client is created, THEN authenticate via `POST /session` with the configured
27	  username/password and send the returned token as the `Cookie` header on every later
28	  request.
29	- WHEN listing styles, THEN page with `skip`/`limit` (page size 200) until a page returns
30	  fewer than `limit` rows, and accept an optional `modified_after` filter for delta pulls.
31	- WHEN a response returns HTTP 500 but carries a valid JSON body, THEN trust the body
32	  (do not treat it as a failure). WHEN a request times out or returns 503, THEN retry
33	  with capped exponential backoff. (Sandbox quirks — see `project_docs/centric_8_api.md`.)
34	- WHEN a reference id (`category_1`, `category_2`, `collection`) is resolved, THEN fetch
35	  the entity (`/category1s/{id}`, `/category2s/{id}`, `/collections/{id}`) and return its
36	  `node_name` (fallback `code`), cached per run. WHEN the id is blank or starts with
37	  `centric%3A`, THEN resolve to empty string without a request.
38	
39	**Refresh / mapping (`loader.py`, refocused Centric → `plm_item`)**
40	- WHEN the refresh runs with `since`, THEN fetch all **active** styles modified at/after
41	  `since`, map each to a `plm_item` record, and upsert them (idempotent, keyed on
42	  `plm_internal_id`). The fetch is **not** gated on `ready_for_wrike` — `ready_for_wrike`
43	  is mapped as a column so 001 reconciliation's *ungated* matching keeps working.
44	- WHEN mapping a style, THEN apply the field map in §3 (incl. `customer` ← `category_2`
45	  resolved, `title` ← `item_number[:8] + " " + node_name`, `modified_at` ← `_modified_at`,
46	  a formula-built `description`), reusing the existing `item_number`-derived `family_id`/
47	  `prefix`/`code` logic.
48	
49	**Producer wiring (`function_app.py`)**
50	- WHEN the producer timer fires, THEN refresh the `plm_item` mirror from Centric
51	  (`since` = current watermark) *before* reading the delta; the rest of the producer
52	  (delta → enqueue one message per canonical family → advance watermark) is unchanged.
53	- WHEN the first run sees no watermark (EPOCH), THEN the refresh pulls the full active
54	  catalogue (one-time backfill); subsequent runs pull only the `modified_after` delta.
55	
56	### Out of Scope
57	
58	- Any change to `plm_reader.py`, `sync.py`, `state.py`, `mapping.py`, `wrike_client.py`,
59	  `changes.py`, the Service Bus producer/consumer flow, or `db/schema.sql` — the engine
60	  and schema from 001 are untouched (`plm_item` already has every needed column).
61	- The consumer or reconciliation calling Centric directly — Centric is touched in exactly
62	  one place (the producer's refresh). The consumer still re-reads `plm_item` by id.
63	- Deleting / deactivating mirror rows when a style goes inactive or is removed in Centric
64	  (no delete propagation — consistent with 001's no-card-deletion stance).
65	- Season resolution (`/seasons` is broken on the sandbox — `season` stays blank).
66	- Two-way sync, webhooks/event-driven pulls, or season-scoped fetching.
67	
68	## 3. Design
69	
70	### Field map: Centric style → `plm_item`
71	
72	| `plm_item` field | Source | Notes |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| `plm_internal_id` | `id` | Centric style id (upsert key) |
75	| `item_number` | `mgf_item_identifier` | |
76	| `item_name` | `node_name` | |
77	| `family_id` / `prefix` / `code` | derived from `item_number` | reuse `item_prefix` + `item_number[:8]` |
78	| `print_method` | `mgf_print_method` | list → join `", "` |
79	| `previous_item_no` | `mgf_previous_item_number` | |
80	| `contents` | `mgf_test_material` | strip HTML |
81	| `material_codes` | `mgf_material_code_item` | |
82	| `brand_category` | `mgf_brand_category_2` | |
83	| `customer` | `category_2` → resolve `/category2s` | e.g. `*CORE` / `*CUSTOM`; drives `pick_canonical` + the create-only "Customer" Wrike field |
84	| `product_category` | `category_1` → resolve `/category1s` | drives author mapping |
85	| `brand` | `collection` → resolve `/collections` | |
86	| `design_request` | `mgf_item_description` | |
87	| `image_link` | `mgf_image_link` | |
88	| `description` | **formula**: section-built from `material_codes` + `contents` | new `build_description()` (§ below) |
89	| `title` | `item_number[:8] + " " + node_name` | |
90	| `ready_for_wrike` | `mgf_ready_for_wrike` | eligibility gate (column, not a fetch filter) |
91	| `modified_at` | `_modified_at` (parsed to timestamptz) | the watermark — Centric's *only* timestamp |
92	| `created_at` | `modified_at` (the parsed `_modified_at`) | the API has **no** creation timestamp (confirmed: only `_modified_at`); reuse the real watermark value, not a dummy. Only feeds `pick_canonical`'s rare no-CORE/no-CUSTOM tiebreak |
93	| `design_brief`, `season`, `status`, `priority`, `end_date`, `folder`, `workflow`, `custom_status` | blank / `None` | not sourced; `None` → omitted from the Wrike payload / Wrike defaults |
94	
95	### Affected Files
96	
97	| Layer | File | Change |
98	|-------|------|--------|
99	| Core logic | `centric_client.py` | **New.** `CentricClient` (session auth, `list_styles(modified_after)`, cached `resolve_ref`) + `make_centric_client()` factory. `requests`-based, mirroring `wrike_client.py`, plus Centric quirks (trust-500-body, retry-on-timeout, `Cookie` auth) |
100	| Core logic | `loader.py` | **Refocus.** Remove the Excel half (`read_source_rows`, `_read_excel_wrike_sheet`, `_read_csv`, `COLUMN_MAP`, `to_plm_item`). Add `style_to_plm_item(style, resolve, *, now)` and `refresh_plm_items(conn, client, *, since, now)`. Keep `item_prefix`, `PLM_ITEM_COLUMNS`, `load_plm_items` (the generic upsert) |
101	| Helpers | `description.py` | Add `build_description(material_codes, contents)` — builds the initial Material Codes / Contents `<h5>` sections for a new card (`merge_description` only *replaces* sections, it can't build them) |
102	| Entry point | `function_app.py` | `plm_wrike_producer`: refresh the mirror from Centric (`since` = watermark) before `sorted_eligible_families`. No other function changes |
103	| Config | `local.settings.json(.example)` | `CENTRIC_*` already present; add optional `CENTRIC_API_VERSION` (default `v2`) |
104	| Deps | `requirements.txt` | Drop `openpyxl` (Excel loader retired). No new runtime dep — use `requests` (already present), **not** the notebook's `httpx`/`pandas`/`dotenv` |
105	| Data | `seed_plm_item.sql`, `data/input/*` | Obsolete once Centric feeds `plm_item`; remove (git keeps history) |
106	| Tests | `tests/test_centric_client.py` (new), `tests/test_loader.py` (rewrite), `tests/fixtures_mapping.py`, `tests/test_reader.py`, `tests/test_description.py` | See Task 6 |
107	| Unchanged | `plm_reader.py`, `sync.py`, `state.py`, `mapping.py`, `wrike_client.py`, `changes.py`, `db/schema.sql` | Engine + schema from 001 untouched |
108	
109	### Key Decisions
110	
111	- **Mirror, not direct read.** `plm_item` stays as a Centric-fed cache. This keeps 001's
112	  "message = pointer, consumer re-reads by id" design intact, keeps reconciliation's
113	  ungated `read_item_customer_pairs` working, and isolates Centric's flakiness (slow
114	  spells, spurious 500s) to a single refresh step instead of the per-message path.
115	- **Refresh inside the producer.** One Centric pull per producer run, `since` = the
116	  current watermark, so the refresh and the existing `modified_at > watermark` delta select
117	  the same rows. EPOCH on the first run ⇒ automatic full backfill.
118	- **Fetch active styles ungated on `ready_for_wrike`.** The mirror must hold not-ready
119	  items too (reconciliation maps cards to PLM records regardless of readiness); gating
120	  happens on the `ready_for_wrike` *column* in the delta, exactly as in 001.
121	- **`requests`, mirroring `wrike_client`.** Same retry/backoff shape; Centric-specific
122	  additions are trust-JSON-body-over-500 and retry-on-timeout. No new dependency.
123	- **`customer` ← resolved `category_2`.** Centric's "Collection" reference holds the
124	  `*CORE`/`*CUSTOM` value, so `pick_canonical` (CORE-over-CUSTOM, latest-updated) is still
125	  meaningful when variants share a `family_id`.
126	- **Timestamps.** Centric exposes only `_modified_at` — no creation date (confirmed against
127	  the spec + a live record). `modified_at` ← `_modified_at` (the watermark); `created_at` ←
128	  the same `_modified_at` (a real timestamp, not a dummy), since it only feeds
129	  `pick_canonical`'s rare fallback. Keeps the engine's column names and leaves
130	  `load_plm_items` + the schema untouched — no rename to `centric_modified_at`/`first_seen_at`,
131	  which would ripple through the otherwise-untouched 001 engine and tests.

```text
1	# Centric 8 REST API — Reference Summary
2	
3	**Source:** [C8 REST API Developer Guide](https://usermanual.wiki/Document/C820REST20API20Developer20Guide.1477580063/html)  
4	**Retrieved:** 2026-06-11  
5	**Version:** V2 (February 2017)  
6	**Status:** *Partially documented from official guide; operational knowledge from sandbox observations included.*
7	
8	## Overview
9	
10	Centric 8 REST API is a resource-oriented HTTP API for integrating Centric PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) with external systems. This project uses it to fetch product styles flagged for Wrike sync, resolve reference fields, and detect changes via modification timestamps. Authentication is session-based; styles are paginated via `skip`/`limit`.
11	
12	## Base Path & Versioning
13	
14	```
15	{CENTRIC_BASE_URL}/csi-requesthandler/api/{version}
16	```
17	
18	- **Base URL example:** `https://company-sandbox.centricsoftware.com`
19	- **Current version:** `v2`
20	- **Fallback:** If `/api/v2` returns 404, try `/api/v1` or `/api/v3`
21	
22	## Authentication
23	
24	### Session Creation (Login)
25	
26	**Endpoint:** `POST /session`
27	
28	**Request Body (JSON):**
29	```json
30	{
31	  "username": "your_username",
32	  "password": "your_password"
33	}
34	```
35	
36	**Response (HTTP 200):**
37	```json
38	{
39	  "token": "session_token_value",
40	  ...other fields...
41	}
42	```
43	
44	**Token Usage:**
45	- Token is returned in response body **and** as an HTTP cookie
46	- On subsequent requests, send token as the `Cookie` header: `Cookie: session_token_value`
47	- Alternatively, some endpoints may accept `Authorization` or `X-Csrf-Token` headers (not documented in official guide; **verify with your instance**)
48	
49	### Session Lifecycle
50	
51	- **Token Validity:** Remains valid for the "session duration configured for your C8 server"
52	- **Expiration:** After token expires, re-authenticate by calling `POST /session` again
53	- **Logout (DELETE):** Call `DELETE /session` to invalidate the current session; server returns HTTP 401
54	- **Concurrent Sessions:** Not explicitly documented; assume one active session per user recommended (standard pattern)
55	
56	### Known Implementation Detail
57	*As-observed on sandbox:* Token is sent as HTTP `Cookie` header, not `Authorization` header. Client libraries must preserve and replay cookies on all subsequent requests.
58	
59	## Listing & Filtering Styles
60	
61	### Endpoint
62	
63	```
64	GET /styles
65	```
66	
67	### Query Parameters
68	
69	| Parameter | Type | Example | Notes |
70	|-----------|------|---------|-------|
71	| `skip` | integer | `0` | Starting offset (pagination). Starts at 0. |
72	| `limit` | integer | `200` | Page size (observed max ~200; default 10). |
73	| `{fieldname}` | string/bool | `mgf_ready_for_wrike=true` | Filter by any field equality. Repeat for AND logic. |
74	| `modified_after` | timestamp | `2026/06/01T00:00:00` | **Documented:** Returns styles modified on or after this time. Format `yyyy/mm/ddThh:mm:ss` (the 2017 guide printed `yyyy/dd/mm`, treated here as a typo — **confirm on your instance**). Critical for incremental sync. |
75	
76	### Pagination Semantics
77	
78	- Loop with `skip` / `limit` until a page returns **fewer than `limit` results**—that's the final page
79	- **As-observed on sandbox:** Page size of 200 is typical; loops terminate when fewer than 200 items received
80	- Response does not include a `total` count field; must iterate to completion
81	- No `next` link in response; must manually construct subsequent URLs
82	
83	### Example Request
84	
85	```bash
86	curl -H "Cookie: <token>" \
87	  "https://company-sandbox.centricsoftware.com/csi-requesthandler/api/v2/styles?mgf_ready_for_wrike=true&skip=0&limit=200"
88	```
89	
90	### Example Response Structure
91	
92	```json
93	[
94	  {
95	    "id": "style-id-123",
96	    "active": true,
97	    "node_name": "Style Name",
98	    "mgf_item_identifier": "ITEM-001",
99	    "mgf_ready_for_wrike": true,
100	    "mgf_print_method": ["print_method_1", "print_method_2"],
101	    "mgf_test_material": "<html>test content</html>",
102	    "mgf_material_code_item": "MAT-CODE-123",
103	    "mgf_brand_category_2": "brand-id-ref",
104	    "category_2": "category-id-ref",
105	    "category_1": "category-id-ref",
106	    "collection": "collection-id-ref",
107	    "mgf_item_description": "Description text",
108	    "mgf_image_link": "https://...",
109	    "mgf_previous_item_number": "PREV-001"
110	  },
111	  ...
112	]
113	```
114	
115	## Incremental/Delta Querying
116	
117	**Status: Officially Documented**
118	
119	Use the `modified_after` parameter to query styles changed since a watermark timestamp:
120	
121	```bash
122	GET /styles?modified_after=2026/06/10T12:00:00&mgf_ready_for_wrike=true&skip=0&limit=200
123	```
124	
125	This is the **recommended method for incremental sync**. Fetch modified styles in batches, update your watermark to the latest timestamp processed, and re-run the query.
126	
127	**Format:** `yyyy/mm/ddThh:mm:ss` (year/month/dayThour:minute:second) — standard order. The
128	2017 guide printed `yyyy/dd/mm`; treated as a typo, **confirm on your instance**.  
129	**Note:** Timezone handling is not explicitly documented; assume UTC or your instance timezone.
130	
131	### No Creation Timestamp (confirmed)
132	
133	`_modified_at` is the **only** timestamp the API exposes. There is no `_created_at` /
134	`created_at` field — confirmed three ways: (1) none of the 751 entity definitions in the
135	spec declare a creation-timestamp field; (2) a live style response has 351 keys whose only
136	underscore-prefixed system fields are `__parent__` and `_modified_at`; (3) `GET
137	/styles?_created_at=…` is silently ignored (returns the unfiltered page). The only key
138	containing "creat" is `created_from_sample`, a reference to a Sample record, not a date. If
139	you need a "first seen"/creation value, stamp it on your own side at ingest. (Centric does
140	hold a true creation date in its internal history — just not via the REST API.)
141	
142	## Reference Resolution
143	
144	Some style fields contain reference IDs (e.g., `category_1`, `collection`, `mgf_brand_category_2`). To resolve them to human-readable names:
145	
146	### Endpoint Pattern
147	
148	```
149	GET /{entity_type_plural}/{id}
150	```
151	
152	### Common Reference Endpoints
153	
154	| Field | Endpoint | Returns |
155	|-------|----------|---------|
156	| `category_1` | `GET /category1s/{id}` | `{"node_name": "...", "code": "...", ...}` |
157	| `category_2` | `GET /category2s/{id}` | `{"node_name": "...", "code": "...", ...}` |
158	| `collection` | `GET /collections/{id}` | `{"node_name": "...", "code": "...", ...}` |
159	| `mgf_brand_category_2` | (typically also `/category2s/{id}`) | — |
160	
161	### Placeholder Values
162	
163	Reference fields may contain:
164	- Empty string `""` (unset reference)
165	- Strings starting with `centric%3A` (URL-encoded `centric:`, a Centric internal namespace marker)
166	- Null or missing in the JSON
167	
168	**Best practice:** Check for these patterns before attempting a resolution request.
169	
170	### Optional Link Header
171	
172	The official guide mentions an optional HTTP `Link` header in requests to include `_links` fields in responses, which maps reference values to their resolution URLs. **Not observed in sandbox usage; verify if your instance supports this.**
173	
174	## Query Syntax & Filtering
175	
176	### Field-Based Filtering
177	
178	Any field can be used as a query filter via equality matching:
179	```bash
180	GET /styles?active=true&mgf_ready_for_wrike=true&category_1=CAT-123
181	```
182	
183	### Documented Operators
184	
185	The developer guide mentions support for "container-based queries," allowing complex queries like:
186	```
187	GET /styles/images?style.parent_season=C3435&tags=front
188	```
189	
190	**Status:** Full operator syntax (range filters, negation, sorting) not documented in publicly available guide. Assume **equality matching only** unless you verify with your instance.
191	
192	### Sorting & Field Selection
193	
194	Not documented in the official guide. **Assume:**
195	- Sorting: Not available via query parameter (request `?sort=field_name` and observe if it works)
196	- Field selection: Not available; API returns all fields
197	
198	## Response Headers & Linking
199	
200	The guide references optional `Link` headers for pagination:
201	```
202	Link: <url_to_next_page>; rel="next", <url_to_last_page>; rel="last"
203	```
204	
205	**As-observed on sandbox:** Not present. Clients must manually construct pagination URLs.
206	
207	## Rate Limits
208	
209	**Not documented in official guide.** Sandbox observations:
210	- **As-observed on sandbox:** No explicit rate-limit headers in responses
211	- **Known server behavior:** API intermittently very slow; use generous timeouts (90+ seconds) and retry on timeout
212	- **Recommendation:** Implement exponential backoff (1s → 2s → 4s → ...) for timeouts and 503s
213	
214	## Error Handling
215	
216	### HTTP Status Codes
217	
218	| Code | Meaning | Typical Action |
219	|------|---------|----------------|
220	| 200 | OK | Success |
221	| 401 | Unauthorized | Session expired or invalid token; re-authenticate |
222	| 404 | Not Found | Endpoint or resource does not exist |
223	| 500 | Internal Server Error | Server error (may resolve on retry) |
224	| 503 | Service Unavailable | Temporary; retry with backoff |
225	
226	### Known Server Quirk
227	
228	**As-observed on sandbox:** Some records return HTTP 500 even though a valid JSON body is included in the response. Callers should **trust the JSON body over the HTTP status code**. Always check if valid JSON is present before treating the error as fatal.
229	
230	### Recommended Error Handling Strategy
231	
232	1. On HTTP 500 with valid JSON body: Parse and use the JSON
233	2. On HTTP 500 with empty body: Retry with exponential backoff
234	3. On timeout: Retry with exponential backoff (90s timeout recommended)
235	4. On HTTP 401: Re-authenticate immediately
236	
237	## Custom Attributes (mgf_*)
238	
239	### Overview
240	
241	Centric allows customers to define custom fields prefixed with `mgf_`. These are **not built-in** and vary by instance configuration. **Example observed fields:**
242	
243	- `mgf_item_identifier` — custom item number
244	- `mgf_ready_for_wrike` — custom boolean flag
245	- `mgf_print_method` — custom list/array
246	- `mgf_test_material` — custom HTML content
247	- `mgf_material_code_item` — custom code reference
248	- `mgf_brand_category_2` — custom category link
249	- `mgf_item_description` — custom description
250	- `mgf_image_link` — custom image URL
251	- `mgf_previous_item_number` — custom legacy identifier
252	
253	### Discovery
254	
255	No automatic schema endpoint is documented. To discover available fields:
256	1. Fetch a sample style: `GET /styles?limit=1`
257	2. Inspect the response for all `mgf_*` keys
258	3. Store the list for field mapping logic
259	
260	## Gotchas / Notes
261	
262	### Session & Timeouts
263	
264	- Server can be **intermittently very slow** (observed on sandbox); use **90+ second timeouts** and retry on timeout
265	- Cookies must be preserved across requests; HTTP client libraries typically handle this automatically
266	- Logout with `DELETE /session` to explicitly invalidate tokens before exiting
267	
268	### Reference Resolution
269	
270	- The `/seasons` endpoint is **broken on the sandbox** (Season references a missing Country enum); season cannot currently be resolved
271	- Placeholder values like `centric%3A...` should be skipped rather than resolved
272	- Always handle missing/null reference fields gracefully
273	
274	### API Version
275	
276	- Official guide is from **February 2017** (V2)
277	- Version V3 may exist; test if `/api/v2` 404s
278	- No versioning information available for features added after 2017
279	
280	### Incremental Sync
281	
282	- **`modified_after` is the primary way to implement delta sync**; there is no alternative streaming or webhook mechanism documented
283	- Timestamp format is `yyyy/mm/ddThh:mm:ss` (standard order; 2017 guide's `yyyy/dd/mm` treated as a typo — verify); verify timezone handling with your instance
284	- No pagination over time windows; always paginate by skip/limit within a date range
285	
286	### Built-In vs Custom Fields
287	
288	- Built-in fields: `id`, `active`, `node_name`, `category_1`, `category_2`, `collection`, etc.
289	- Custom fields: All `mgf_*` prefixed fields (instance-specific)
290	- No canonical list of built-in attributes available; discover by fetching samples
291	
292	## References
293	
294	- [Centric 8 REST API Developer Guide (HTML)](https://usermanual.wiki/Document/C820REST20API20Developer20Guide.1477580063/html)
295	- [Centric 8 REST API Developer Guide (PDF)](https://usermanual.wiki/Document/C820REST20API20Developer20Guide.1477580063.pdf) — Version 2, Rev 1, February 2017
296	- [Centric Software Official](https://www.centricsoftware.com)
297
```

```md
# PLM to Wrike Sync

One-way synchronisation of product data from a PLM source database into Wrike work items.
The pipeline runs as three Azure Functions (two core sync functions plus a reconciliation function)
decoupled by an Azure Service Bus queue, so each record is processed and retried independently
and a single bad record never stops the batch.

## What it does

- Reads product records that changed since the last run from a PostgreSQL source table.
- Selects one canonical record per product family (CORE preferred over CUSTOM).
- Creates a Wrike card for a new family, or updates the existing card for a known family via a
  1:1 live map (PLM record ↔ Wrike card keyed by id).
- On update, writes only the fields that actually changed, merges the PLM-owned description
  sections, comments on tracked content changes, and raises a comment-only alert on fields
  that must not be auto-overwritten.
- Routes unmapped or ambiguous cards to a human-reviewed log table, exported to Excel for
  data-quality review.
- Records the outcome of every record in a sync-state table and routes repeated failures to
  a dead-letter queue.

The sync is one directional, from PLM to Wrike. Wrike is never read back as a source of truth
beyond confirming the current state of a card before an update.

## Architecture

\```
Centric 8 PLM API
   -> Producer Function (timer)        refreshes plm_item mirror, reads change delta, enqueues messages
   -> PostgreSQL (plm_item mirror)     local cache of active Centric styles (read by producer/consumer/reconcile)
   -> Service Bus queue (plm-sync)     decouples and buffers, with a dead-letter queue
   -> Consumer Function (queue trigger) transforms and writes to Wrike, records sync state
   -> Wrike API                        creates or updates the card
   -> PostgreSQL (sync state)          family to card map, watermark, dead-letter, unmapped log
   -> Reconciliation Function (HTTP)   on-demand full-folder audit of unmapped cards
\```

| Azure resource | Role |
|---|---|
| Function App (Python) | Hosts three functions: producer (timer), consumer (queue trigger), reconciliation (HTTP) |
| Service Bus namespace and queue | Decoupling, retry, and dead-lettering between producer and consumer |
| PostgreSQL | Centric mirror (`plm_item`), sync state, live map, folder routing, and unmapped-card log |
| Key Vault | Wrike tokens, Centric credentials, database connection string, Service Bus connection string |
| Application Insights | Execution logs, failures, and queue metrics |

## How it works

### Producer (timer trigger)

Runs on a schedule (`0 0 12,0 * * *`, which is 12:00 and 00:00 UTC, or 05:00 and 17:00
Pacific). On each run it:

1. Reads the watermark (last run timestamp).
2. Refreshes the `plm_item` mirror from Centric: fetches all active styles modified since the
   watermark, maps each to a `plm_item` record (resolving references, joining lists, stripping
   HTML), and upserts them. On the first run, this is a full backfill of the active catalogue.
3. Selects records where `modified_at` is later than the watermark and the eligibility flag
   (`ready_for_wrike`) is set.
4. Reduces each family to its canonical record.
5. Sends one Service Bus message per family. The message carries identifiers only, not a data
   snapshot, so the consumer always acts on the current database state.
6. Advances the watermark once the messages are enqueued. Delivery and retry are then owned by
   the queue.

The producer does not call Wrike.

### Consumer (Service Bus queue trigger)

Triggers once per message. For each message it:

1. Re-reads the canonical family by identifier. If the family is no longer eligible, the
   message is acknowledged and skipped.
2. Decides create or update using a three-step resolution:
   - If the family has a live map row, update that card directly by id (no Wrike search).
   - Otherwise, search Wrike by the "PLM - Item #" custom field within the prefix's mapped folder.
   - Branch based on the search result: nothing → create; one exact match → update; extras or
     non-exact → log to the review table.
3. Builds the Wrike payload and writes the card (if the branch is create or update).
4. Records the result in the sync-state table and the unmapped-log table (if applicable).

An unhandled error abandons the message lock, so Service Bus redelivers it and, after the
maximum delivery count, moves it to the dead-letter queue.

### Reconciliation (HTTP trigger, on demand)

The `plm_wrike_reconcile` function (route `/api/reconcile`, auth level FUNCTION) performs a
full-folder audit: it walks every card in each managed folder (including the staging folder)
and attempts to match each card to a PLM record by item number + raw customer string. Cards
that do not match—including hand-made cards—are logged to the unmapped-log table for the
client's data-quality review. The function is read-only against Wrike and run on demand
(e.g., after a cold-start or to audit the folder state).

## Field mapping and sync rules

- Create payload carries the full field set. Update payload carries only update-eligible
  custom fields whose incoming value differs from the live card.
- Create-only fields (for example brand category, customer, design brief, image link) are set
  once at creation and never overwritten on update.
- The description is section-merged on update, not replaced. Only the PLM-owned sections are
  refreshed.
- A change to a tracked content field (material codes, contents) is written and a summary
  comment is added to the card.
- A change to a protected field (title, brand category) is not written. A comment-only alert
  is posted instead.
- Every new card is stamped with the Wrike Item Type "Retail Item".
- A card with no real change is left untouched.
- Customer matching is raw and exact (no normalization)—deliberately surfaces data-quality
  issues so they land in the Excel export for client review.

The Wrike author of a card is the owner of the API token that created it. Tokens are mapped to
product categories in the `category_author_map` table. Cards are placed in the folder identified
by the `wrike_folder_map` table (prefix → folder id), and a family with an unmapped prefix is
created in the staging folder (a special `'*'` row in `wrike_folder_map`) and the missed prefix
is logged.

## Data model

The schema is defined in `db/schema.sql`.

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `plm_item` | Local mirror of active Centric styles (refreshed from Centric API on each producer run) |
| `category_author_map` | Product category to author token mapping |
| `sync_watermark` | Incremental cursor and last-run statistics |
| `wrike_task_map` | 1:1 live map (PLM record ↔ Wrike card); keys: `plm_internal_id` (PK) ↔ `wrike_task_id` (UNIQUE); columns `item_number`, `family_id`, `customer` for audit/recovery |
| `wrike_folder_map` | Item prefix to folder routing table (human-maintained, sole authority); keys: `prefix` (PK), columns `wrike_folder_id`, `full_folder_name`, `space_id`, timestamps |
| `wrike_unmapped_log` | Review log for unmapped, ambiguous, or hand-made cards; columns: `item_number`, `customer`, `wrike_task_id`, `prefix`, `reason` (e.g., `no_exact_match`, `multiple_exact_matches`, `non_identical_extra`, `unmapped_prefix`, `no_plm_match`), `details`, `created_at` |
| `sync_dlq` | Records that failed after retries |

## Configuration

All configuration is supplied through Function App application settings. Secrets are stored in
Key Vault and referenced from the settings, so no secret value is held in the application
configuration itself.

| Setting | Purpose | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `PG_CONN` | PostgreSQL connection string | Key Vault reference |
| `ServiceBusConnection` | Queue listener connection (consumer) | Key Vault reference |
| `ServiceBusSendConnection` | Queue sender connection (producer) | Key Vault reference |
| `ServiceBusQueue` | Queue name, default `plm-sync` | Plain value |
| `CENTRIC_BASE_URL` | Centric 8 API base URL (e.g., `https://company-sandbox.centricsoftware.com`) | Plain value |
| `CENTRIC_USERNAME` | Centric API user account | Key Vault reference |
| `CENTRIC_PASSWORD` | Centric API user password | Key Vault reference |
| `CENTRIC_API_VERSION` | Centric API version, default `v2` | Plain value |
| `WRIKE_TOKEN_<NAME>` | Wrike API token per author identity | Key Vault reference |
| `WRIKE_HOST` | Wrike API host, default `www.wrike.com` | Plain value |
| `WRIKE_RETAIL_ITEM_TYPE_ID` | Custom Item Type id for new cards | Plain value |
| `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` | Telemetry | Plain value |

The `WRIKE_TOKEN_<NAME>` setting names must match the `token_ref` values in
`category_author_map`. Folder routing is read from the `wrike_folder_map` table; the app
never searches Wrike for folders by name. A special `'*'` row in `wrike_folder_map` serves as
a fallback staging folder for unmapped prefixes. If no `'*'` row is present, items with
unmapped prefixes defer (safe degradation).

For details on Centric authentication and the field mapping from Centric to `plm_item`, see
`project_docs/centric_8_api.md` and `specs/002-centric-8-api-source.md`.

## Deployment using the Azure portal

1. Resource group. Create a resource group to hold all resources.

2. PostgreSQL. Create an Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. Apply `db/schema.sql`
   to create the tables.

3. Service Bus. Create a Service Bus namespace on the Standard tier. Add a queue named
   `plm-sync` and set maximum delivery count to 10, enable dead-lettering on message
   expiration, and enable duplicate detection. The dead-letter queue is created automatically.

4. Key Vault. Create a Key Vault. Add the Centric credentials, Wrike tokens, the PostgreSQL
   connection string, and the Service Bus connection string as secrets.

5. Function App. Create a Function App with the Python runtime. Open Identity and enable the
   system-assigned managed identity. In the Key Vault access policies, grant that identity Get
   and List on secrets.

6. Application settings. Open Configuration on the Function App and add the settings in the
   table above. For each secret, use a Key Vault reference of the form
   `@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/secrets/<name>/)`.

7. Networking, if the database is private. Add VNet integration on the Function App and place
   the database behind a network rule that allows access from the function subnet only.

8. Deploy the code. Publish this project to the Function App using the Azure Functions
   extension for Visual Studio Code, the Azure Functions Core Tools, or the portal Deployment
   Center. After deployment, three functions appear under Functions: `plm_wrike_producer`
   (timer), `plm_wrike_consumer` (queue trigger), and `plm_wrike_reconcile` (HTTP).

9. Folder mapping. Populate the `wrike_folder_map` table with the item prefixes and their
   target folder ids (e.g., WP → 4459532498, LT → 4469574468). New prefixes are added by
   humans after client/business approval, not by the app.

10. Verify. On the Function App, confirm the host is running and all three functions are listed.
    On Configuration, confirm every Key Vault reference shows a resolved status. Test the
    producer and consumer by running the producer manually (via Code and Test or admin endpoint)
    and checking the queue depth and logs.

## Operations

- Run on demand. The producer runs automatically on its schedule. To run it immediately,
  open the `plm_wrike_producer` function in the portal and use Code and Test, then Run, or
  call the function admin endpoint with the host key. `scripts/trigger_azure.sh` wraps the
  command-line equivalents for triggering, checking queue depth, and tailing logs.

- Reconciliation audit. To audit the managed folders for unmapped or hand-made cards,
  call the `plm_wrike_reconcile` HTTP function (route `/api/reconcile`). The function is
  read-only and logs every unmapped card to the review table for export.

- Monitor. Use Application Insights for execution logs and failures. Use the Service Bus
  metrics for active and dead-lettered message counts.

- Failures. A record that fails all retries lands in the queue dead-letter sub-queue and is
  recorded in `sync_dlq`. Configure an alert on a dead-letter count greater than zero so a
  record that never reached Wrike is noticed.

- Data-quality review. Export the `wrike_unmapped_log` table to Excel to review unmapped,
  ambiguous, and hand-made cards. The table includes the item number, customer, Wrike task id,
  prefix, reason code, and details for each unmapped card.

## Local development

A local environment is provided for running the test suite. It is not required for the Azure
deployment.

1. Set up a local PostgreSQL instance with a `plm` database and `plm` role. The defaults
   are `localhost:5432`, `db plm`, `user plm`, `password plm_local_pw`. To override, set
   any of `PG_HOST`, `PG_PORT`, `PG_DB`, `PG_USER`, `PG_PASSWORD`, or use a single `PG_CONN`
   connection string.

2. Apply the schema (idempotent, includes guarded migrations):

\```
psql -h localhost -U plm -d plm -f db/schema.sql
\```

3. Optionally load the sample data:

\```
psql -h localhost -U plm -d plm -f seed_plm_item.sql
\```

4. Run the test suite:

\```
python -m pytest
\```

Tests automatically skip database-backed cases if PostgreSQL is unreachable. Note that tests
truncate the state tables during execution. Before running a live sync batch after tests,
reload the seed data to reset the sync state.

The application reads settings locally from `local.settings.json`, which is excluded from
version control. Use `local.settings.json.example` as a template. To run the producer locally
(e.g., to test a Centric refresh), populate the Centric settings in `local.settings.json`.

```

```text
1	# Azure Deployment Runbook — PLM → Wrike (Service Bus architecture)
2	
3	**What this is:** the exact, replayable steps used to deploy the full architecture to Azure
4	on 2026-06-03, including the real gotchas hit on a personal subscription and how they were
5	fixed. Pairs with the design in [`azure_deployment_guide_2026-06-03.md`](azure_deployment_guide_2026-06-03.md)
6	and the smoke test in [`smoke_test_steps.md`](smoke_test_steps.md).
7	
8	Target deployed (resource group `rg-wrike-poc`, region `eastus`):
9	- VM `vm-plm-pg` (private PostgreSQL 16, source DB) — *Stage 1*
10	- Function App `func-wrike-poc-pk` (Flex Consumption) hosting `plm_wrike_producer` (timer)
11	  + `plm_wrike_consumer` (Service Bus trigger) — *Stages 2 & 4*
12	- Service Bus namespace `sb-wrike-poc-pk` + queue `plm-sync` — *Stage 3*
13	- Key Vault `kv-wrike-poc-pk` — *Stage 6*
14	- VNet `vnet-wrike` + `snet-db`/`snet-func` + NSG `nsg-db` — *Stage 7*
15	
16	> Auth is **Path A** (Service Bus connection string in Key Vault) to fit the Contributor
17	> role. See the guide for the Managed Identity (Path B) upgrade.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 0. Prerequisites
22	
23	```bash
24	az version          # Azure CLI (used 2.86)
25	func --version      # Azure Functions Core Tools v4 (used 4.10)
26	az login            # interactive; device-code if headless: az login --use-device-code
27	az account show     # confirm the right subscription
28	```
29	
30	**Register the resource providers you'll use** (this was the single biggest gotcha — see
31	§Gotchas). Registration is async; wait for `Registered`:
32	
33	```bash
34	for p in Microsoft.Compute Microsoft.KeyVault Microsoft.ServiceBus Microsoft.Web Microsoft.Network; do
35	  az provider register --namespace $p
36	done
37	# verify, e.g.:
38	az provider show -n Microsoft.Compute --query registrationState -o tsv   # must be "Registered"
39	```
40	
41	Set shared variables:
42	
43	```bash
44	RG=rg-wrike-poc; LOC=eastus
45	SB_NS=sb-wrike-poc-pk; QUEUE=plm-sync
46	KV=kv-wrike-poc-pk
47	VNET=vnet-wrike
48	APP=func-wrike-poc-pk
49	az group create -n $RG -l $LOC
50	```
51	
52	## 1. Service Bus queue (Stage 3)
53	
54	```bash
55	# namespace (skip if it already exists)
56	az servicebus namespace create -g $RG -n $SB_NS -l $LOC --sku Standard
57	# queue — NOTE the flag is --enable-duplicate-detection (NOT --requires-duplicate-detection)
58	az servicebus queue create -g $RG --namespace-name $SB_NS -n $QUEUE \
59	  --max-delivery-count 10 --lock-duration PT5M \
60	  --enable-dead-lettering-on-message-expiration true \
61	  --enable-duplicate-detection true \
62	  --duplicate-detection-history-time-window PT10M
63	```
64	
65	## 2. VNet, subnets, NSG (Stage 7)
66	
67	```bash
68	az network vnet create -g $RG -n $VNET -l $LOC \
69	  --address-prefix 10.20.0.0/16 --subnet-name snet-db --subnet-prefix 10.20.1.0/24
70	# Function integration subnet — delegated to Microsoft.App/environments for Flex Consumption
71	az network vnet subnet create -g $RG --vnet-name $VNET -n snet-func \
72	  --address-prefixes 10.20.2.0/24 --delegations Microsoft.App/environments
73	# NSG: allow Postgres only from the function subnet
74	az network nsg create -g $RG -n nsg-db -l $LOC
75	az network nsg rule create -g $RG --nsg-name nsg-db -n allow-pg-from-func \
76	  --priority 100 --direction Inbound --access Allow --protocol Tcp \
77	  --destination-port-ranges 5432 --source-address-prefixes 10.20.2.0/24
78	az network vnet subnet update -g $RG --vnet-name $VNET -n snet-db --network-security-group nsg-db
79	```
80	
81	## 3. Key Vault + secrets (Stage 6)
82	
83	```bash
84	# access-policy mode (NOT rbac) so a Contributor can grant secret access without role assignments
85	az keyvault create -g $RG -n $KV -l $LOC --enable-rbac-authorization false
86	ME=$(az ad signed-in-user show --query id -o tsv)
87	az keyvault set-policy -n $KV --object-id $ME --secret-permissions get list set delete
88	
89	# Wrike tokens (from local.settings.json), Service Bus connection string, DB conn (added in step 5)
90	SBCONN=$(az servicebus namespace authorization-rule keys list -g $RG --namespace-name $SB_NS \
91	  -n RootManageSharedAccessKey --query primaryConnectionString -o tsv)
92	az keyvault secret set --vault-name $KV -n WRIKE-TOKEN-PRAVEEN --value "<token>"
93	az keyvault secret set --vault-name $KV -n WRIKE-TOKEN-JESSE   --value "<token>"
94	az keyvault secret set --vault-name $KV -n ServiceBusConnection     --value "$SBCONN"
95	az keyvault secret set --vault-name $KV -n ServiceBusSendConnection --value "$SBCONN"
96	```
97	
98	## 4. VM for PostgreSQL (Stage 1)
99	
100	Capacity/SKU notes (see §Gotchas): on this subscription eastus had capacity only for the
101	**B-family in zone 1**. Pick a SKU+zone that is unrestricted for your subscription:
102	
103	```bash
104	# inspect what is actually available before creating:
105	az vm list-skus -l $LOC --resource-type virtualMachines --all -o json \
106	 | python -c "import sys,json;[print(s['name'],[r['type'] for r in s.get('restrictions',[])]) for s in json.load(sys.stdin) if s['name'] in ('Standard_B2s','Standard_DS1_v2')]"
107	
108	# create — private, NO public IP, in snet-db; pin the zone that has capacity
109	az vm create -g $RG -n vm-plm-pg \
110	  --image Ubuntu2204 --size Standard_B2s --zone 1 \
111	  --vnet-name $VNET --subnet snet-db \
112	  --public-ip-address "" --nsg "" \
113	  --admin-username azureuser --generate-ssh-keys
114	```
115	
116	## 5. Install + seed PostgreSQL on the VM (no SSH, no public IP)
117	
118	The DB is private, so manage it with `az vm run-command` (runs over the Azure fabric).
119	
120	**5a. Generate the seed SQL locally as UTF-8** (gotcha: Windows `python > file` writes cp1252):
121	
122	```bash
123	PYTHONUTF8=1 python scripts/gen_seed_sql.py > db/_seed_plm_item.sql
124	python -c "open('db/_seed_plm_item.sql','rb').read().decode('utf-8'); print('valid utf-8')"
125	```
126	
127	**5b. Install PostgreSQL 16, configure, apply schema + seed** via a single run-command
128	script (`scripts/` contains the assembled version; the essential steps it performs):
129	
130	```bash
131	# the script installs PGDG postgresql-16, sets listen_addresses='*',
132	# adds pg_hba rules for 10.20.2.0/24 (func) + 10.20.1.0/24, creates role+db 'plm',
133	# then applies db/schema.sql and db/_seed_plm_item.sql, and prints the row count.
134	az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm-plm-pg --command-id RunShellScript \
135	  --scripts @/tmp/vm_setup.sh --query "value[0].message" -o tsv
136	# expect: ROWCOUNT=11  FAMILIES=11
137	```
138	
139	**5c. Store the DB connection string** (VM private IP from `az vm create` output, e.g. 10.20.1.4):
140	
141	```bash
142	az keyvault secret set --vault-name $KV -n PG-CONN \
143	  --value "host=10.20.1.4 port=5432 dbname=plm user=plm password=<pw>"
144	```
145	
146	## 6. Configure + deploy the Function App (Stages 2 & 4)
147	
148	```bash
149	# managed identity + Key Vault access (so KV references resolve)
150	PID=$(az functionapp identity assign -g $RG -n $APP --query principalId -o tsv)
151	az keyvault set-policy -n $KV --object-id $PID --secret-permissions get list
152	
153	# VNet integration to the function subnet (so it can reach the private DB)
154	az functionapp vnet-integration add -g $RG -n $APP --vnet $VNET --subnet snet-func
155	
156	# app settings — Key Vault references + non-secret config
157	ref(){ echo "@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=https://$KV.vault.azure.net/secrets/$1/)"; }
158	az functionapp config appsettings set -g $RG -n $APP --settings \
159	  "ServiceBusConnection=$(ref ServiceBusConnection)" \
160	  "ServiceBusSendConnection=$(ref ServiceBusSendConnection)" \
161	  "ServiceBusQueue=$QUEUE" \
162	  "PG_CONN=$(ref PG-CONN)" \
163	  "WRIKE_TOKEN_PRAVEEN=$(ref WRIKE-TOKEN-PRAVEEN)" \
164	  "WRIKE_TOKEN_JESSE=$(ref WRIKE-TOKEN-JESSE)" \
165	  "WRIKE_HOST=www.wrike.com" \
166	  "WRIKE_FOLDER_WP=4459532498" "WRIKE_FOLDER_LT=4469574468" \
167	  "WRIKE_RETAIL_ITEM_TYPE_ID=IEAF5GXSPIABGBNX"
168	
169	# deploy code (remote build)
170	func azure functionapp publish $APP --python
171	```
172	
173	## 7. Verify the deployment (non-destructive — no Wrike cards)
174	
175	```bash
176	SUB=$(az account show --query id -o tsv)
177	# all Key Vault references must say "Resolved"
178	az rest --method get --url "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$SUB/resourceGroups/$RG/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/$APP/config/configreferences/appsettings?api-version=2022-03-01" \
179	 | python -c "import sys,json;[print(i['name'],i['properties']['status']) for i in json.load(sys.stdin)['value']]"
180	# DB has 11 rows
181	az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm-plm-pg --command-id RunShellScript \
182	  --scripts "sudo -u postgres psql -d plm -tAc 'SELECT count(*) FROM plm_item'" --query "value[0].message" -o tsv
183	```
184	
185	**Before any live run, confirm the Wrike target folders are the intended space** (Personal,
186	not production). Resolve `WRIKE_FOLDER_*` ids and check their parent space via the Wrike API
187	(`GET /folders/{id}` → `parentIds`; `GET /spaces/{id}/folders` to confirm membership).
188	
189	## 8. Smoke test
190	
191	See [`smoke_test_steps.md`](smoke_test_steps.md): trigger `plm_wrike_producer` via the admin
192	endpoint, watch `plm-sync` drain, confirm 11 rows in `wrike_task_map` and 11 cards in Wrike.
193	
194	---
195	
196	## Gotchas hit on this subscription (and fixes)
197	
198	| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
199	|---|---|---|
200	| VM create fails `QuotaExceeded — Current Limit: 0`; **Usage+quotas page blank**; `az vm list-usage` returns 0 entries | **`Microsoft.Compute` provider not registered** | `az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Compute`; default PAYG quota (10 cores) appears once Registered |
201	| VM create fails `SkuNotAvailable / Capacity Restrictions` for B1ms/B2s/DS1_v2 (regionally) | eastus capacity-constrained for those SKUs on this sub | Inspect `az vm list-skus … restrictions`; B-family was open in **zone 1** only → `--size Standard_B2s --zone 1` |
202	| `az postgres flexible-server create` fails `The location is restricted from performing this operation` | Managed Postgres region-restricted in eastus for this sub (works in eastus2) | Used a **VM-hosted Postgres** instead (the chosen full-arch design anyway) |
203	| Seed load fails `invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0xa0` | Windows `python > file` wrote SQL as cp1252; a non-breaking space became a lone 0xA0 | Regenerate with `PYTHONUTF8=1`; validate it `.decode('utf-8')` cleanly |
204	| `az servicebus queue create … --requires-duplicate-detection` → `unrecognized arguments` | Flag renamed | Use `--enable-duplicate-detection true` |
205	| `az … 2>&1 | tail` shows only a `RuntimeError: content already consumed` traceback | CLI error-formatting bug masks the real error when piped | Don't `tail` the failing command; `grep -iE "error|restricted|quota"` the full output |
206	| Function can't be loaded from a private DB by your laptop | DB has no public endpoint | Manage/seed the DB via `az vm run-command` (Azure fabric, no inbound network) |
207	| KV secret writes blocked under Contributor | RBAC-mode vault needs role assignments | Create vault with `--enable-rbac-authorization false` (access-policy mode) |
208	
209	---
210	
211	## Teardown (bring cost to ~$0)
212	
213	Pause (reversible, keeps everything; resume in a minute):
214	
215	```bash
216	az vm deallocate -g $RG -n vm-plm-pg          # stops the main compute cost
217	az functionapp stop -g $RG -n $APP            # halts the twice-daily timer
218	# resume: az vm start … ; az functionapp start …
219	```
220	
221	Full teardown of what this deployment added (run after detaching VNet integration):
222	
223	```bash
224	az functionapp vnet-integration remove -g $RG -n $APP
225	DISK=$(az vm show -g $RG -n vm-plm-pg --query storageProfile.osDisk.managedDisk.id -o tsv)
226	NIC=$(az vm show -g $RG -n vm-plm-pg --query networkProfile.networkInterfaces[0].id -o tsv)
227	az vm delete -g $RG -n vm-plm-pg --yes
228	az network nic delete --ids "$NIC"
229	az disk delete --ids "$DISK" --yes
230	az network vnet delete -g $RG -n $VNET
231	az network nsg delete -g $RG -n nsg-db
232	az keyvault delete -g $RG -n $KV               # soft-deleted 90 days (no cost); purge to free the name
233	az servicebus namespace delete -g $RG -n $SB_NS   # removes the queue too (~$10/mo Standard tier)
234	```
235	
236	> The Function App (Flex Consumption), its storage account, and App Insights cost ≈ $0 when
237	> idle/stopped, so they can be left in place or deleted to taste.
238
```
</details></tool-use>

36	KEY=$(az functionapp keys list -g $RG -n $APP --query masterKey -o tsv)
37	curl -s -i -X POST "https://$HOST/admin/functions/plm_wrike_producer" \
38	     -H "x-functions-key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}'
39	```
40	
41	Expect **HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted**. The producer reads the 11 changed families from the
42	private Postgres and sends one message each to `plm-sync`.
43	
44	## Step 2 — watch the queue drain as the consumer processes
45	
46	```bash
47	az servicebus queue show -g $RG --namespace-name $NS -n plm-sync \
48	  --query "countDetails" -o jsonc
49	```
50	
51	Run it a few times. You'll see `activeMessageCount` rise toward 11 and then fall back to 0
52	as `plm_wrike_consumer` creates each card. `deadLetterMessageCount` should stay **0**.
53	
54	## Step 3 — verify the sync results in the database
55	
56	The DB is private, so query it through the VM (no password needed — peer auth as postgres):
57	
58	```bash
59	az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm-plm-pg --command-id RunShellScript \
60	  --scripts "sudo -u postgres psql -d plm -tAc \"SELECT family_id, wrike_task_id, sync_status FROM wrike_task_map ORDER BY family_id\"" \
61	  --query "value[0].message" -o tsv
62	```
63	
64	Expect **11 rows**, each with a `wrike_task_id` and `sync_status = created`.
65	
66	## Step 4 — verify in Wrike
67	
68	Open the **WP** and **LT** folders in Wrike. You should see the 11 new cards (6 WP, 5 LT),
69	each with **Item Type = Retail Item** and the PLM custom fields populated.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## Troubleshooting
74	
75	- **Live logs (consumer):** Portal → `func-wrike-poc-pk` → Monitor → Logs / Live Metrics
76	  (Application Insights). Or try `az webapp log tail -g $RG -n $APP`.
77	- **Dead-lettered messages** (`deadLetterMessageCount > 0`): a record failed all retries.
78	  Inspect the consumer logs for the exception. The message body is in `plm-sync/$DeadLetterQueue`.
79	- **202 but nothing enqueues:** the producer found nothing changed (watermark already past
80	  the rows). Reset it — see below.
81	
82	## Re-run from a clean slate
83	
84	Resets the watermark and the family→card map so the producer re-enqueues all 11:
85	
86	```bash
87	az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm-plm-pg --command-id RunShellScript \
88	  --scripts "sudo -u postgres psql -d plm -c \"TRUNCATE sync_watermark, wrike_task_map, sync_dlq\"" \
89	  --query "value[0].message" -o tsv
90	```
91	
92	Then repeat Step 1. Note: cards already in Wrike are **found by title search and updated**
93	(no duplicates) — to see fresh *creates* again, delete the 11 cards in Wrike first.
94	
95	## Note on the twice-daily timer
96	
97	`plm_wrike_producer` also runs automatically on its schedule (`0 0 12,0 * * *` = 05:00 /
98	17:00 PT). Step 1 just triggers it on demand so you don't have to wait.
99
```
</details></tool-use>
